text: Capturing moments is what photography is all about, whether it's a candid shot of a family gathering or a serene sunset. Aperture and shutter are the key elements that determine how much light enters the camera and how much is reflected back, respectively. A wide aperture allows more light to enter, while a smaller aperture (smaller f-number) captures more detail and depth. The shutter speed controls the duration of exposure and helps to achieve the desired exposure settings. The combination of aperture and shutter is called exposure, which is an essential element in capturing stunning photos.
